title: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz type II
summary: The PR interval stays the same, then a P wave suddenly fails to conduct. The block is below the AV node.
source: Slides 34, 36-38 (Mobitz type II, 2:1 block, high-grade block)

events.label: Conducted beat
events.caption: An impulse passes through the AV node and the His-Purkinje system.

events.label: Same PR again
events.caption: The next beat conducts with exactly the same delay.

events.label: Still the same
events.caption: The block is not in the AV node, so the PR does not lengthen as the beats go on.

events.label: Sudden block
events.caption: Without warning an impulse is blocked below the AV node, in the His-Purkinje system, which cannot conduct it so soon after the last one.
events.ecg: A P wave with no QRS, and no earlier lengthening of the PR.

events.label: Conduction resumes
events.caption: The next impulse conducts normally.
events.ecg: The PR interval is the same as before the dropped beat.

teaching_points: Mobitz type II: the PR interval is constant and a QRS is dropped suddenly (slide 34); the block is almost always infranodal.
It can progress suddenly to complete heart block, so it is treated more seriously than type I.
With 2:1 block the ECG alone cannot tell type I from type II: look at the QRS width and the response to atropine or exercise (slide 37).
